documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy
documents.summary: The college-wide Academic Honesty Policy in the Student Handbook is mostly procedure (reporting, hearings, sanctions). Its only AI content is one clause that lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' as a breach of academic integrity on independent work.
documents.stance_why: The only AI text is 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence', named as an example of misrepresenting others' ideas or language as one's own; AI is thus barred unless approved, which is restrict. The document does not say who approves or set any tiers.

units.why: The clause lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among forms of representing the ideas or language of others as one's own on independently prepared work, so AI use without approval is an integrity violation. It binds students, sets a standard (general phase), bans AI absent approval (must-not, restrict), and P36 fits because it classifies AI misuse as an integrity violation; P06 does not fit because the clause does not say what applies when a syllabus is silent.
units.anchor: unapproved use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: In projects and assignments (including homework)
units.frag_end: resubmitted personal work for another course.
units.policy: Unapproved use of artificial intelligence on projects and assignments prepared independently is an example of representing the ideas or language of others as one's own, which breaches the College's standards of honesty and academic integrity.

documents.summary: The Computer Science department sets four tiers of AI use, from none to completely open, and each CS course falls under one tier. It is a pilot for Fall 2026 and the department plans to revisit it regularly. Use outside a course's tier counts as an honor policy violation.
documents.stance_why: The document offers four tiers ('0. Absolutely no usage allowed' to '3. Completely open use') for each course to adopt, so the department itself sets no single stance and delegates to the course.

units.why: States the purpose is 'a unified system' to clarify allowed and disallowed AI uses 'across all Pomona Computer Science classes'. It is a department-level preamble giving purpose and scope, so P56 and informs; the tier structure itself is coded in a later unit as P05.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P05 with actor all; coder B coded P56 with actor admin. The source sentence is headed 'Purpose of this document' and states why the department provides a unified system and over what scope, which is the P56 definition (framework preamble stating purpose and scope). The tier definitions themselves are a separate sentence and carry P05. The text is a department statement, so the actor is admin.

units.frag_start: To provide a unified system
units.frag_end: across all Pomona Computer Science classes.

units.why: Says the system is a pilot in Fall 2026 and 'we plan to revisit it regularly', a commitment to review, so P54 and over-time.

documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy (Computer Science Department)
documents.summary: The Computer Science department Academic Honesty Policy sets general rules for individual work, collaboration, exams, course materials and penalties. Its AI content says AI tools count as unapproved help and refers to the department AI Policy Tier System, which each course follows.
documents.stance_why: The text bars sources 'other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools' but then says 'all Computer Science courses will now follow' the AI Policy Tier System, with exceptions 'in the course syllabus'. The actual stance is handed to each course's tier, so delegates; the page points to the tiers rather than offering them, so tiers is left empty.

units.why: Work submitted must be 'completed independently, unless collaboration on a particular assignment is explicitly permitted'. This is a rule that submitted work is the student's own (P29), must. The next sentences apply it to AI.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this sentence. It is a real rule (independent work, unless collaboration is permitted) and sets up the AI sentences that follow, so it is kept. It does not name AI, so unit_stance is neutral rather than B's restrict.
units.anchor: the work you submit must be completed independently
units.frag_start: However, the work you submit

units.why: Submitted work must not be based on 'information obtained from sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools'. AI is out unless approved, which is the 'unless approved, not allowed' pattern of P06; P19 is narrower (producing the work).
units.resolution_why: A coded P01, B coded P06. The sentence does not ban AI outright: it bans sources 'other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools', so AI is barred unless an instructor approves it. That is the 'unless allowed, prohibited' fallback rule of P06; P01 is a ban on AI on graded work, which this is not unconditionally.
